# Uninstaller

> Removes the bundle plus every associated file, to the Trash only, with matching precise enough not to sweep up a sibling app.

Canonical page: https://anishfyi.com/mac-uninstaller/
Source: https://github.com/anishfyi/mac-uninstaller
Download: https://github.com/anishfyi/mac-uninstaller/releases/latest
Author: Anish Kr Singh (anishfyi), https://anishfyi.com/

## What it is

A fast native macOS app that removes an application plus every leftover file across ~/Library, and reclaims space from orphaned support files, caches and logs. Everything goes to the Trash, never deleted outright.

## Facts

- Finds the app bundle plus every associated file across ~/Library, including Application Support, Caches, Preferences, Logs, Saved State, Containers and Group Containers, shows them with sizes, and moves the selected ones to the Trash in one click.
- Everything goes to the Trash via FileManager.trashItem and is never deleted outright, so any removal can be restored until the Trash is emptied.
- Association is by exact bundle id or a dot-bounded prefix or suffix, never a bare substring, so a sibling like com.foo.barbecue is not swept up with com.foo.bar. Folders merely named after an app are shown but left unchecked.
- Apple bundle ids (com.apple.*) and shared identifiers are never offered for removal.
- A Cleanup tab reclaims space from three sources: orphaned leftovers whose app is gone, regenerable caches in ~/Library/Caches, and logs, diagnostic reports and crash reports.
- Explicit confirmation on item count and total size before anything moves.
- Built in SwiftUI for Apple silicon, macOS 14 or later.

## Questions and answers

### What is Uninstaller?

Uninstaller is a fast, native macOS app that removes an application and all of its leftover files, plus a Cleanup panel that reclaims space from orphaned support files, caches and logs.

### Is it safe to remove files with Uninstaller?

Everything it removes goes to the Trash using FileManager.trashItem rather than being deleted outright, so anything can be restored until you empty the Trash. It also asks for explicit confirmation on item count and total size before moving anything.

### Will it delete files belonging to a different app?

No. Association is by exact bundle id or a dot-bounded prefix or suffix, never a bare substring, so com.foo.barbecue is never swept up when you uninstall com.foo.bar. Folders merely named after an app are shown but left unchecked for you to confirm.

### What does the Cleanup tab do?

It scans for three kinds of reclaimable space: orphaned leftovers whose app is no longer installed, regenerable data in ~/Library/Caches, and logs, diagnostic reports and crash reports.

### What are the system requirements?

Apple silicon running macOS 14 or later. A few protected folders such as Safari, Mail and Messages data need Full Disk Access to scan.

### Does Uninstaller touch system files?

No. Apple bundle ids (com.apple.*) and shared identifiers are never offered for removal.
